title: MAI Code 2 Pricing: Plans, Seats, and Token Costs (2026)
summary: MAI Code 2 pricing structures for 2026 help development teams select the appropriate subscription tier based on their monthly token consumption needs.
body_markdown:
## Translating MAI Code 2 credits into real-world usage


The true cost of development is hidden behind a proprietary credit system. It obscures how much work your team can actually complete before the bill spikes.


> The true cost of development is hidden behind a proprietary credit system.


This abstraction makes it impossible to predict monthly expenses. A single task might consume a handful of credits or thousands depending on the underlying model's current price.


### Credit cost of a complex code refactor


When a deep architectural change is required, the platform must ingest your entire codebase and generate hundreds of lines of logic. This process drains credits faster than simple autocomplete.


Vandatateam's analysis puts the credit cost per request for high-reasoning models like Claude Opus 5.5 at a level that increases significantly.


A single afternoon of heavy refactoring can exhaust a junior developer's entire monthly allocation. This means teams exceeding their allotment are charged overage fees immediately, rather than being forced to pause work until the next billing cycle refreshes.


### Rate limits and concurrency by plan tier


Your ability to run multiple automated tests at once is strictly governed by your subscription level. It dictates how many requests the platform will process per minute.


On the entry-level tiers, the system throttles your connection if three or more developers push code simultaneously.


The run is the meter, not the steps inside it. Activepieces charges 1 credit per flow run regardless of how many steps are executed, which contrasts with the per-module billing found in other platforms.


This allows teams to build highly granular, multi-step code review processes without being penalized for the complexity of their logic.


Your CI/CD pipeline sits idle while waiting for a slot to open. To achieve the instant feedback required for modern deployment, you must move to higher-priced seats regardless of whether you need the extra features.


### Context window size and credit burn rate


Models like Gemini 4 Carbon can see more of your project at once thanks to large context windows. Every additional file sent in that window multiplies the credits consumed for that single interaction.


Because the platform charges for every line of code maintained in the model's memory, a developer working on a large enterprise application burns through their budget ten times faster than one working on a standalone script.


This creates a financial penalty for following best practices like providing the AI with full project context to ensure code consistency.
